claims.text: The target material is solidified, equiatomic, Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The as-solidified FeNiCrMn microstructure inherently provides a balanced combination of strength and ductility.
Dynamic behavior in as-solidified FeNiCrMn is governed by temperature-modulated activation of specific dislocation slip systems.
Localized stacking-fault formation is a governing deformation process in dynamic FeNiCrMn.
Dynamic-recovery features concurrently contribute to governing the dynamic response of FeNiCrMn.
Dislocation slip, stacking faults, and dynamic recovery together maintain FeNiCrMn's strength–ductility balance.
Temperature changes the activation barriers for dislocation slip and stacking-fault formation.
Lower temperature or higher strain rate restricts dislocation mobility in FeNiCrMn.
Restricted dislocation mobility increases dislocation nucleation and entanglement, thereby increasing strength.
Higher temperature enhances dynamic recovery, facilitates dislocation motion, and mitigates dislocation accumulation.
Enhanced dynamic recovery preserves ductility while retaining adequate strength.
At high strain rates or low temperatures, FeNiCrMn will exhibit increased dislocation density and limited dynamic recovery.
At high strain rates or low temperatures, localized stacking faults will become more pronounced.
At elevated temperatures, dynamic recovery will become more active and stacking-fault features less pronounced.
Severe adiabatic shear banding can arise under high-rate or large-deformation loading and represents a competing mechanism outside the proposed boundary.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes regimes in which severe adiabatic shear banding or other defect-induced mechanisms occur, but the falsification rule treats dominance of localized shear banding as evidence that falsifies the hypothesis. The same observation is therefore presented both as outside the hypothesis's scope and as a valid falsifier.
